A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SIL/ASGDRO research and contain corresponding main sections and appendices A.1–A.11. Their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v3 reports original ASGDRO experiments on H-CMNIST and distribution-shift benchmarks, together with Grad-CAM and Hessian analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical studies and additionally reports standalone ASGDRO results on DomainBed in Table 4.

M1.justification: The ASGDRO objective, adaptive perturbation and group-loss reweighting remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 makes the environment loop explicit, while Section 3.5 expands implementation explanations. The shared empirical-risk perturbation was already described in v3 Section 4.3.

E1.justification: Both retain the same H-CMNIST feature-removal scenarios, subpopulation benchmarks, WILDS tasks, five DomainBed datasets and appendix MetaShift/Multi-NLI evaluations. Standalone ASGDRO adds a configuration within existing dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator sets are retained. PDE disappears from main Table 2 but remains in Appendix Table 5 with identical results for the same comparison. The new SAGM citation supplies experimental setup information rather than an additional evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Table 4 adds standalone ASGDRO evaluation alongside the retained DPLCLIP configurations. Appendix A.9 identifies a separate setup through Wang et al.'s work, without detailing it locally. Previously stated splits, metrics, training budgets and hyperparameter searches remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The toy loss-surface study, H-CMNIST feature-removal tests, Grad-CAM cases and Hessian analyses are retained unchanged. v4 newly points to appendix efficiency/sensitivity analyses, but the supplied appendix contains no corresponding analyses or results.

E5.justification: The retained experiments preserve their three-seed reporting and existing mean/dispersion summaries. No revised run counts, uncertainty-estimation procedures or significance tests are documented. The changed RxRx1 dispersion value is a numerical result update.

E6.justification: Table 4 adds standalone ASGDRO results across five DomainBed datasets, averaging 65.9. Table 3 changes its RxRx1 accuracy from 30.5±0.1% to 32.2±0.2%, above the retained FeAT–ERM result of 30.7±0.4%. Figure 7 still reports 30.5±0.1%, leaving the update internally inconsistent. Other matched results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 explicitly states a linear model with orthogonal features and replaces the robust-risk/gradient-penalty equality with an approximation (v3 Equation 6; v4 Equation 4). This qualifies the formal statement; Appendix A.4 largely retains the existing derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: SIL for diverse invariant features, ASGDRO through common flat minima, and the H-CMNIST benchmark. Additional DomainBed evidence supports these existing claims.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 drops v3's observation that defining individual invariant-feature subsets can itself be ambiguous, retaining the intervention-cost concern. The main mechanism interpretations and Appendix A.1 limitations concerning computational overhead and synthetic benchmark validation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 adds an author-code repository link in the abstract, explicitly specifies the normalization matrix in Section 3.5, and clarifies Algorithm 1's environment loop. Appendix A.9 adds a setup citation and repository pointer for standalone DomainBed evaluation.

R1.justification: v4 adds Chen et al. on Pareto IRM, Lin et al. on spurious-feature diversification, and Wang et al. on sharpness-aware gradient matching. Section 2.1 specifically distinguishes multiple spurious features from SIL's multiple invariant features. These are localized additions to the existing positioning.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify Sections 3.1–3.2, move shared-perturbation implementation text from Section 4.3 to 3.5, and expand Appendix A.6 explanations. v4 also adds author contact information and acknowledgements and adopts numbered citations; the main section and appendix sequence remains intact.

P2.justification: The predominantly single-column manuscript becomes a two-column main paper and reference list, with extensive resizing and repositioning of displays and wider appendix layouts. All nine figure images are retained, but their presentation changes substantially. Table 2 omits the duplicated PDE row, and Table 4 adds a standalone ASGDRO row.

improvement.justification: The explicit normalization specification, code-access information and standalone DomainBed evaluation modestly improve documentation and empirical support. Theorem 1 also states its restrictions and approximation more clearly, although its proof is largely unchanged. These benefits are tempered by the new Table 3/Figure 7 RxRx1 inconsistency and the unsupported pointer to appendix efficiency/sensitivity analyses.
